title: Binomial coefficient vanishing forces a prime-power exponent
statement: Let $p$ be a prime integer and let $d>0$ be an integer. If $p\mid\binom{d}{r}$ for every integer $r$ with $0<r<d$, then there exists an integer $a\ge0$ such that $d=p^a$. Here $\binom{d}{r}=d!/(r!(d-r)!)$ is the integer binomial coefficient, with the binomial-coefficient notation of [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] for the commutative ring $\mathbf Z$.
